unsecured objects.

Blountstown, Bristol, Altha, Rock Bluff, Moose Pond, Clarksville,
Ocheesee, Selman, Abe Springs, Hosford, Chipola, Henderson Mill,
Kennys Mill, Lowry, Blountstown Airport, Hugh Creek, Red Oak,

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Caroline, MD; Kent, MD; Queen Anne's, MD
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Caroline County in eastern Maryland...
Southwestern Kent County in northeastern Maryland...
Central Queen Anne's County in northeastern Maryland...

* Until 1045 AM EDT.

* At 640 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets, and underpasses as well as other
drainage and low lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Centerville, Centreville, Church Hill, Carville, Starkey Corner,
Hope, Starr, Old Town, Overton and Queenstown.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Missouri, including the following
county, Scott.

* WHEN...Until 845 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 537 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sikeston, Scott City, Chaffee, Oran, Miner, Benton, Morley,
Kelso, Hay-Wood City, Cape Girardeau Airport, Vanduser,
Blodgett, Diehlstadt, Commerce and Lambert.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: St. Andrews Bay Waterways; Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out 20 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
St. Andrews Bay Waterways...

* Until 615 AM CDT.

* At 521 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 12 nm south of Panama City Beach, moving
northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Kelleys Island in Erie County in North Central Ohio

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Remaining standing water and flooding of low-lying and
poor-drainage areas from overnight rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 546 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated gauges indicated
that 7 to 14 inches of rain fell across Kelleys Island
overnight. Flash flooding was reported overnight. Flash
flooding no longer poses an imminent threat to life and
property, but residual standing water and flooding of low-
lying and poor-draiange areas continues this morning.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Kelleys Island.

- Please visit www.weather.gov/safety/flood for flood safety
and preparedness information.
